title: There is no epidemic of loneliness, but there is an epidemic of scurvy
summary: This thought-provoking article challenges the modern framing of loneliness as an 'epidemic' by drawing a historical parallel with scurvy, suggesting that while loneliness is a real issue, the current discourse may overstate the problem or underprovide practical solutions compared to how historical societies addressed actual nutritional diseases.
problem_solved: Questions whether modern society's response to loneliness matches the seriousness of the problem, or if the 'epidemic' framing is more rhetorical than substantive.
why_valuable: Offers a critical historical perspective that encourages readers to question contemporary health narratives and consider whether we address modern social issues with the same urgency as historical physical diseases.
